correctness.rationale: For the repaired claim: symmetry gives B⊆T²(B) and antitonicity gives T³=T. The first-image indicators depend on disjoint bits except at Hamming distance two, where two bits are shared; this yields the exact moments and the stated local-dependence inputs. The repair uses a conservative process bound from AGG Theorem 3; it does not need the sharper original constant. The pair union bound is O_c(d^4/2^d). For any separated S, each external site has at most two neighbors in N(S) since it cannot be at distance two from two sites in S. With d≥3 this proves T²(S)=S, and disjoint neighborhoods give the exact companion size. When (d+1)|S|<N, the sparse phase uniquely identifies the primitive orbit. The fixed-m census follows from the same distance test on a uniform m-set. At p=1/2+c/d the count is tight with the specified Poisson limit; the separation and Markov estimates show that the first image is the strictly smaller phase with probability tending to one, not an almost-sure assertion across dimensions. The all-zero state supplies exactly the extra r^N in the universal-orbit basin. At fixed interior p, the mean or relative variance gives the two claimed limiting regimes.
residual_risks: The finite verifier does not establish the selection limit or certify a full deterministic orbit census. No claim about an almost-sure coupling across dimensions or an optimal Poisson error constant is made.

originality.rationale: Only for the repaired claim. The frozen framing treated the cube first-image Poisson scaling and universal-orbit curve as part of the distinct contribution. In fact the time-one zero field in the distinct open-neighbor OR record is exactly the NOR first image on the same initial bits. The Gumbel-shaped universal-basin limit follows directly from that coverage law and the basin identity; different dynamics do not make the law independent. The repair gives explicit credit and restricts the distinct contribution to the separated NOR sparse phases, their dense companions, primitive orbit census and the mass selecting that family. The available matching statements do not establish that geometry or census. No chronological order between same-date records is inferred.
residual_risks: The Nor/OR overlap is mathematical, not a finding of date priority. The bounded search did not rule out other separated-code constructions for NOR or a stronger attractor classification.
